items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes quasi-compact objects of a site by a finiteness property of surjections onto the sheaf represented by the object: such a surjection from a coproduct of sheaves admits a finite subfamily which is still surjective (statement lines 3520-3531). The proof is a complete equivalence: the first implication follows the identity section through the description of a coproduct of sheaves as a sheafified coproduct, refines the covering and uses quasi-compactness to obtain a covering with finite image, which yields the finite subfamily (proof lines 3534-3554); the converse turns a covering into a surjection from a coproduct of representable sheaves, applies the hypothesis to get a finite subfamily and produces the required members by a section argument (proof lines 3556-3578). The non-formal content is the passage between sections of a coproduct and single summands. The claim is H2: two written-out implications with each input named.
